en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: The aim of the course is to provide a comprehensive overview of microbiological, biochemical, molecular biological and immunological methods for the diagnosis of pathologically important microorganisms in human and veterinary medicine.

en.label: [section] Course content:
en.content: 1.Introduction (allowance 2/0) a.History, significance and overview of methodological approaches for diagnosis of microorganisms.b.Safety of work with pathogenic agents.c.Division of microbiological laboratories according to safety levels.2.Culture and staining techniques and biochemical tests for the diagnosis/classification of bacterial pathogens (allowance 2/0)3.Cultivation diagnostic methods in virology and use of experimental animals (allowance 2/0)4.Microscopic techniques (use of light and electron microscopy for diagnosis of microorganisms) (allowance 2/0)5.Immunological diagnostic methods (allowance 6/0) a.Precipitation and agglutination tests, complement-fixation reactions, neutralization tests.b.ELISA, its formats and applications.c.Fluorescent and chemiluminescent immunoassays, dip-stick techniques and western blotting6.Diagnostic methods based on biosensor and biochip technologies (allowance 2/0)7.Electromigration techniques used in diagnosis and classification of microorganisms (allowance 2/0)8.Mass spectrometric techniques (allowance 2/0)9.Molecular biology methods (allowance 6/0) a.Pulsed gel electrophoresis, restriction analysis, hybridization techniques.b.PCR and other diagnostic methods based on signal amplification.c.Mobile genetic element analysis, plasmid profile analysis, antibiotic resistance marker analysis, ribotyping.10.Alternative methods for diagnosis of microorganisms (allowance 2/0)
